name: K'AP TÁI SHAP
description: K'ap Tái Shap (Big Collecting Tens) is an expanded version of K'ap Shap, designed for larger groups (up to 20 players) and utilizing multiple sets of Chinese dominoes (up to 8 sets). It is a high-stakes, fast-paced game where the goal is to form a specific combination of identical pairs and 10/20-sum pairs. The use of multiple sets introduces high duplication, changing the strategy from simple matching to probability-based hoarding.

content.text: K'ap Tái Shap (Big Collecting Tens) is an expanded version of K'ap Shap, designed for larger groups (up to 20 players) and utilizing multiple sets of Chinese dominoes (up to 8 sets). It is a high-stakes, fast-paced game where the goal is to form a specific combination of identical pairs and 10/20-sum pairs. The use of multiple sets introduces high duplication, changing the strategy from simple matching to probability-based hoarding.
Developed as a social club variant of K'ap Shap in Hong Kong and Guangdong, where large groups needed a game that could accommodate everyone at a single table.
Usually one set per every 2-3 players. For 10 players, 4 sets (128 tiles) is standard.
Multiple sets of Chinese dominoes, flat playing surface, chips or counters for stakes
Standard 10/9 tile split. Tiles are shuffled face-down and built into a long wall (the 'Dragon').

items.text: Ch'i Tái Shap: A variant with 'Seven Big Sets' using 7 sets of dominoes.
Wild K'ap: A version where the Red Soldiers (from Xiangqi) are added as wildcards.
K'ap Shap (Small): The standard 32-tile two-player version.
